What Is Financial Planning For Retirement? A Beginner’s Guide
Hoping for financial security or to maintain your current lifestyle post working days? Here's how you should proceed, keeping your goals in mind.
Planning a financially secure retirement is an extremely important exercise in today’s world. While a part of your routine and existence for decades, the professional life ends at some stage, and then the next challenge is to ensure you can sustain your livelihood. Therefore, designing a financial roadmap that allows you to spend the rest of your life comfortably is critical. But take no stress, we’ve got you covered. Here’s how you can break down the task of financial planning for your retirement.
Identify Your Post Retirement Goals
Recommended Stories
There are different goals for different people when it comes to post-retirement financial planning. The most common is to ensure financial independence when you’re no longer working professionally and earning a salary. Some aim to secure or maintain their current lifestyles without letting the financial fall affect their standards.
When you hit the retirement age, focusing on your health should be a priority. Working professionals undergo retirement planning to ensure they have sufficient coverage for healthcare and emergencies. Others want to leave behind enough wealth and a legacy for their family members to remember fondly.
Once your goals for retirement planning are ascertained, it is important to identify the different factors that could influence your path ahead. Estimating future needs is one of them. Those nudging on the retirement age usually reassess their expenses, travel, hobbies and how much inflation they might confront in the future. The age you want to retire and the life you wish to live thereafter. This is where prudent investing comes into play.
Saving And Investment Tools For Post Retirement Planning
Identifying different tools to invest and safeguard your finances for post-retirement plans should be the next step for individuals. The good thing is that today we have different options or tools to forge our investment plans around. These tools include provident funds, pension schemes and mutual funds and asset investment in financial markets.
Retiring individuals can opt for a tool depending on their specific aims, keeping in mind the risk involved and whether the tool gives them significant health, life and long-term financial care. Below is a breakdown of the schemes and tools that can help you safeguard your retirement life.
Government Schemes: National Pension System (NPS), Employment Provident Fund (EPF)
Private Investments: Mutual Funds, SIPs, Fixed Deposits
Insurance: Pension Plans, Life & Health Insurance Coverage
Assets: Investing in Real Estate, Gold, Stocks
